newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF sees growth in 1997 outside Europe.
newsitem.headline: SKF sees growth in 1997 outside Europe.

text.p: Swedish bearings manufacturer SKF AB said on Thursday it expected increased demand for its products in 1997 through continued growth in markets outside Western Europe.
Releasing its 1996 results, SKF said it saw weaker demand from Western Europe in the fourth quarter of 1996 and saw no pick-up this year although it did not expect the situation to worsen.
"Demand for the group is expected to increase during 1997 through continued growth in markets outside Western Europe," SKF's managing director Peter Augustsson said in a statement.
"No additional downturns are anticipated in Western Europe but as yet there are no signs of an upturn."
SKF posted a 29 percent drop in its profits for calendar 1996.
It reported a profit after financial items of 2.41 billion crowns compared to 3.39 billion crowns in 1995.
Sales fell by 8.5 percent to 33.59 billion crowns.
"Changes in exchange rates had an adverse effect corresposding to 7.5 percent, or 2.66 billion crowns of reported sales, when translated into Swedish crown," SKF said.
